column3: The Hebrew commands girding the loins and explicitly taking the oil in the hand; BSB paraphrases the clothing action and leaves the hand implicit.
The Hebrew calls the companions brothers and repeats a room within a room; BSB uses companions and an inner room.
The Hebrew expresses the anointing as completed; BSB uses a present “I anoint.”
The Hebrew repeats the word for young man before prophet; BSB condenses this to young prophet.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves both actors unnamed, repeats the two designations of the people, and expresses anointing as completed; BSB names Jehu and the young prophet.
The Hebrew joins the vengeance with “and,” without a separate verb for blood being shed.
The Hebrew retains a man urinating against a wall, the restrained and the abandoned; BSB has every male, slave and free.
The Hebrew repeats house for each dynasty; BSB combines the latter houses in a plural.
The Hebrew leaves the door opener unnamed; BSB supplies the young prophet.
The Hebrew has a singular questioner and says this man and his speech; BSB uses plural speakers and his kind and their babble.
The Hebrew leaves the respondent unnamed and expresses anointing as completed; BSB supplies Jehu and a present anointing.
The Hebrew leaves the recipient of the garments unnamed; BSB supplies Jehu.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew retains the soul of the addressed group without explicitly naming commanders or making him king; BSB supplies both.
The Hebrew has a riding verb without explicitly naming a chariot in this verse.
The Hebrew uses an ordinary saying verb for Joram and has a brief “Is there peace?”; BSB uses commanded and an arrival question.
The Hebrew asks what peace is to the rider, not what he knows about peace.
The Hebrew leaves the sender unnamed; BSB supplies the king. Jehu asks what peace is to the rider.
The Hebrew names the driving, not a separate charioteer.
The Hebrew has a singular unnamed harnessing agent; BSB uses plural “they.” It separately repeats their going out.
The Hebrew names Jezebel’s whoredoms; BSB has idolatry.
The Hebrew explicitly says Joram turned his hands.
The Hebrew retains filling the hand with the bow and names the arms, then the arrow coming out from the heart.
The Hebrew leaves Jehu unnamed; BSB supplies his name.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives the command to strike him in the chariot at the ascent but no separate clause saying they shot Ahaziah; BSB adds that action.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says she looked through the window, without explicitly naming downward direction.
